pieces.title: Fuzuli, gazel «Öyle ser-mestem ki idrâk etmezem dünyâ nedir» (from Leylâ vü Mecnûn), bayts 1, 2, 4, 5 (maqta)
pieces.author: Muhammad Fuzuli (Mahammad Füzuli)
pieces.text:
öyle ser-mestem ki idrâk etmezem dünyâ nedir
men kimem sâkî olan kimdir mey û sahbâ nedir
gerçi cânândan dil-i şeydâ içün kâm isterem
sorsa cânân bilmezem kâm-ı dil-i şeydâ nedir
hikmet-i dünyâ vü mâfiha bilen arif degil
arif oldur bilmeye dünyâ vü mâfiha nedir
ah u feryâdın fuzûlî incidipdir âlemi
ger belâ-yı aşk ile hoşnûd isen kavga nedir.
pieces.notes:
The text is the artist's own Turkish caption track on the official video, copied verbatim. It is the published text for this exact recording. All three sources have the same words and the same order of bayts; only the spelling differs.

The arrangement sings bayts 1, 2, 4 and 5. Bayt 3 is never sung. In tr.wikisource it reads: «Vasldan çün âşıkı müstağnî eyler bir visal / Âşıka mâşukdan her dem bu istiğna nedür».

tr.wikisource (no named source; edited by anonymous users, last change 2025-05-05) has these forms:
- «Ben kimem sâki olan kimdir mey ü sahbâ nedir»
- «Gerçi cânândan dil-i şeydâ için kâm isterem / Sorsa cânan bilmezem kâm-ı dil-i şeydâ nedir»
- «Hikmet-i dünya vü mâfiha bilen ârif degül / Ârif oldur bilmeye dünya vü mâfiha nedür»
- «Âh u feryâdun Fuzûlî incidübdür âlemi / Ger belâ-yı ışk ile hoşnûd isen gavga nedür ….»

az.wikisource (source: Anar, «Min beş yüz ilin oğuz şeri», Bakı 1999) has:
- «Öylə sərməstəm ki, idrak etməzəm dünya nədir, / Mən kiməm, saqi olan kimdir, meyü-səhba nədir.»
- «Gərçi canandan dili-şeydam üçün kam istərəm, / Sorsa canan bilməzəm kami-dili-şeyda nədir.»
- «Hıkməti-dünyavi-mafihə bilən arif deyil, / Arif oldur bilməyə dünyavi-mafiha nədir.»
- «Ahü fəryadım, Füzuli, incidibdir aləmi, / Gər bəlayi-eşq ilə xoşnud isən, qovğa nədir?»

The earlier draft doubted the reading of bayt 4: bilmeye or kim bile. All three sources read bilmeye / bilməyə, and none of the sources read here has «kim bile».

The official credit says «Azerbaijani words by Mahammad Fuzuli». The caption track is labelled Turkish and uses an Ottoman-Turkish transcription with Azerbaijani-leaning forms: «men», «içün», «incidipdir». The caption spelling has its own quirks: «mâfiha» without the long marks, «arif» without â, «degil», and a closing period after «kavga nedir». It is kept here as published.

Whisper heard «Ben kim…» at 47 s, where the official caption has «men kimem». Check this by ear.

The Arabic-script «alt» lines in the earlier draft have no source.

Verification 2026-10-17: the az.wikisource URL in otherSources is the populated page (title uses dünya nedir; oldid 95847). A different title with nədir is an empty page. The Doğan 2000 wording was read from the Kayaokay PDF (Littera Turca 10(3), 2024), not from the book. Quotation begins «Eyle ser-mestem» and ends «gavgâ nedür (Doğan, 2000: 475-476)». Footnote 2 on belâ-yı says some copies read Kerbelâ-yı; sung captions and the opened texts read belâ. A space in «mâ-fî hâ» may be a PDF line-break; the next hemistich in the same quotation is «mâ-fîhâ». The book page itself was not opened. Archive.org TOC labels p. 473 as Mecnun Dilinden Gazel and p. 475 as Söz Sonu. The Anar 1999 PDF was not opened; the archive filename says Nazim Ibrahimov. No Arabic-script edition was found. Sung orthography remains the caption track, one source: VTT bodies could not be re-downloaded on 2026-10-17.

pieces.title: Hildegard of Bingen, antiphon for the Holy Spirit «Karitas habundat in omnia» (Symphonia)
pieces.author: Hildegard of Bingen
pieces.text:
Karitas
habundat in omnia,
de imis excellentissima
super sidera
atque amantissima
in omnia,
quia summo regi osculum pacis
dedit.
pieces.notes:
Hildegard Society: «Latin collated from the transcription of Beverly Lomer and the edition of Barbara Newman». Manuscripts: D 157r, R 466v.

Cantus DB, Dendermonde f. 157r, Cantus ID a00528. Source spelling: «Caritas habundat in omnia de imis excellentissima super sidera atque amantissima in omnia quia summo regi osculum pacis dedit». The indexing notes say the initial «C» is missing in the manuscript. The words are identical to the Hildegard Society text; only Karitas/Caritas differs.

The official captions do not print the Latin. Each choir passage is split into the same six cues in the Turkish, Arabic and English tracks, so the sung lines are mapped by translation:
1. Karitas habundat in omnia
2. de imis excellentissima
3. super sidera
4. atque amantissima
5. in omnia
6. quia summo regi osculum pacis dedit

The whole antiphon is sung in each passage. In cue 5 the Turkish track has «her şeyde, her şeyde», which may mean «in omnia» is sung twice. Check by ear.

Official credit: «Latin words by Hildegard von Bingen».

Verification 2026-10-17: cantus.uwaterloo.ca/chant/588605 redirects to cantusdatabase.org/chant/588605. Source spelling re-read there: Caritas, habundat, regi lowercase, one «in omnia» in each place. The manuscript image was not opened. Newman 1988/1998 was not opened; the Society collation is the cited text. English and Arabic caption tracks were not re-downloaded. nasheedlyrics (a mirror, not an independent source) prints English «in all» once and an Arabic rendering of cue 5 once; only the Turkish cue doubles «her şeyde». Doubling of sung Latin in omnia stays unconfirmed. Latin dedit is active; the Turkish cue is passive verilmiştir.

pieces.title: al-Shushtari, «Yā sāqiya l-qawmi min shadhāhu», bayt 1
pieces.author: Abu al-Hasan al-Shushtari
pieces.text:
يا ساقيَ القَومِ مِن شَذاهُ
الكلُّ لمَّا سَقيتَ تاهُوا
pieces.notes:
The harakat are as printed in the official Arabic caption track (466.89–509.80 s). Only the first bayt is sung.

The poem in poetsgate and in adab.wiki (موسوعة الأدب العربي, «ثمانية» abyat; both texts identical):
يا ساقيَ القَوْم من شَذاه / الكلُّ لمَّا سَقيْت تاهوا
عاتَبو وبالسُّكرِ فيك طابوا / وصرَّحوا بالهوى وفاهُوا
ما شِربَ الكاسَ واحتساهُ / إِلا محِبُّ قدِ اصطفاهُ
يا عاذِلي خلِّني وشُرْبي / فلسْت تدري الشراب ماهُو
…

The words agree; only the vowel marks differ. The caption has القَومِ and سَقيتَ, while poetsgate has القَوْم and سَقيْت.

The official description names al-Shushtari as one of the two mawwal poets. Only these two sources were read; no printed diwan of al-Shushtari was checked.

Verification 2026-10-17: aldiwan poem 69336 was opened (8 abyat). Opening: يا ساقيَ القَوْم من شَذاه / الكلُّ لمَّا سَقيْت تاهوا. Printed diwan page https://ablibrary.net/book_content/b/9579/80 was opened (eds. al-Numayri, al-Adluni, Abu al-Fuyud), under the heading يا من هو هو. Opening there: يا ساقي القوم من شذاه / الكلّ لمّا سقيت تاهوا. Bayt 1 words agree. The next bayt begins عاتبوه on the printed page and عاتَبو on aldiwan. Nashshar's critical diwan was not opened. Sung harakat remain the caption's. The earlier note that no printed diwan was checked is superseded for this page.

pieces.title: al-Nabulsi, «ʿAynī li-ghayri jamālikum lā tanẓuru», bayt 1
pieces.author: Abd al-Ghani al-Nabulsi
pieces.text:
عَيني لغيرِ جمالِكُم لا تَنظُرُ
و سِواكُم في خاطِري لا يَخطُرُ
pieces.notes:
Copied verbatim from the official Arabic caption track (509.80 and 520.64 s), including the space in «و سِواكُم».

ar.wikisource has the poem in 10 abyat. Its opening:
عيني لغير جمالكم لا تنظر \\ وسواكمو في خاطري لا يخطر
وجميع فكري فيكمو دون الورى \\ وعلى محبتكم أموت وأحشر
يا سادة قلبي بهم متعلق \\ أبدا وعنكم ساعة لا أصبر
The Harvard page gives the same 10 abyat.

The sung text has وسواكم where the editions have وسواكمو.

The official Sami Yusuf short (-5qOGo_ai0E) attributes these lines to «Abd al-Ghani al-Nabulsi (1641–1731)». The Harvard page notes that al-Nabulsi built the poem on two older verses that are also found at the end of the Dīwān of ʿAfīf al-Dīn al-Tilimsānī.

Verification 2026-10-17: ar.wikisource oldid 475413 and the Harvard page https://sites.harvard.edu/sulaymanibnqiddees/2023/09/01/my-eyes-only-see-your-beauty/ were the texts used. Both have وسواكمو and do not contain the sabbartu bayt. Sung form remains the caption و سِواكُم. poetsgate was not reopened.

pieces.title: Mawwal bayt «Ṣabbartu qalbī ʿalaykum fa-ajābanī / lā ṣabra lī…»
pieces.author: attributed to Abd al-Ghani al-Nabulsi by the official release; the close variant is in the poem of ʿAfīf al-Dīn al-Tilimsānī
pieces.text:
صَبَّرتُ قَلبي عَليكُم فأجَابني
لا صَبرَ لِي، لا صَبرَ لِي، كَيفَ أصبِرُ؟
pieces.notes:
The words are verbatim from the official Arabic caption (529.88 and 539.87 s). Whisper heard «La sabrali, la sabrali, keyfe asbi» at 540.14–545.90 s, which agrees.

This bayt is not in al-Nabulsi's poem as printed in ar.wikisource, poetsgate or the Harvard page.

The nearest verse is in al-Tilimsani's poem on the same opening line (Harvard page): «شاورتُ قلبي بعدكم فأجابني. *** لا صبر لي لا صبر لي كيف أصبِر». Its second hemistich matches the sung one; its first hemistich differs.

Sung folk versions of the mawwal reportedly have «صبرت قلبي عنكم فأجابني / لا صبر لي لا صبر لي لا أصبر». This was seen only as a search snippet and was not read.

The official short translates: «My heart has awaited you, answer me; I have no patience, no patience—how can I be patient?»

Verification 2026-10-17: still one source for the sung words (captions; Whisper agrees on the second hemistich). Authorship unchanged: official short says al-Nabulsi; the printed 10-bayt poem does not contain this first hemistich; Tilimsani on the Harvard page has شاورتُ قلبي بعدكم and the same second hemistich. The short pages returned HTTP 500 from Invidious on 2026-10-17 and were not re-read as HTML.

openQuestions: The official captions cover the voice map only in part. Nothing is captioned in these voiced stretches: 2–35, 301–363 (short phrases), 550–632, 687–705, 714–721, 733–750, 760–813, 835–861 and 942–977 s. They may be wordless vocalise, unpublished text, or erhu/ney/violin leaking into the Demucs vocal stem. They must be checked by ear before any text is placed there.
Fuzuli pronunciation: the official caption has «men kimem», «içün», «degil», «nedir». Whisper heard «Ben kim…» at 47 s. The site follows the caption; check «men» against «ben» by ear.
Hildegard cue 5 («in omnia»): the Turkish caption says «her şeyde, her şeyde», and the earlier draft had «omnia, omnia». Check whether the choir repeats «in omnia».

Who sings what is not stated anywhere except Ahmed Elmaai for the al-Nabulsi lines. Hildegard = Cappella Amsterdam and Fuzuli = Sami Yusuf are inferences. Also unconfirmed: whether the choir doubles the «hikmet» repeats or the final reprise, and whether Ahmed Elmaai also sings the al-Shushtari lines (467–510 s).

The earlier draft claimed a contrapuntal finale with Hildegard and Fuzuli sung together. The captions show them in sequence: Hildegard twice at 879–921 s, then Fuzuli bayts 1–2 at 921–942 s. Overlap is possible only if heard.

The bayt «صَبَّرتُ قَلبي عَليكُم فأجَابني / لا صَبرَ لِي، لا صَبرَ لِي، كَيفَ أصبِرُ؟» is attributed to al-Nabulsi only by the official short. It is not in his poem as printed in ar.wikisource, poetsgate or the Harvard page. The closest printed form is in al-Tilimsani: «شاورتُ قلبي بعدكم فأجابني. *** لا صبر لي لا صبر لي كيف أصبِر». A printed dīwān of al-Nabulsi or al-Tilimsani is needed to settle authorship. Until then, show it as «по официальному релизу — ан-Набулуси» with a caveat.
The al-Shushtari poem «يا ساقي القوم من شذاه» was checked only on poetsgate and adab.wiki (identical texts, probably one origin). A printed Shushtari dīwān (e.g. ed. al-Nashshar) would firm it up.
The Arabic-script Fuzuli lines («alt») in the earlier draft have no source. Find an edition (Akyüz et al., Fuzûlî Dîvânı, or Leylâ vü Mecnûn) or drop them.

Personnel not credited: the violin soloist, any Amsterdam Andalusian Orchestra members besides Ahmed Elmaai, the conductor or musical director, and which oudist plays the oud solo. The names in the earlier draft «Mohamed al-Mokhlis» and «Haytham Safia» appear in no official credit; do not use them.
The streaming release (JioSaavn) lasts 15:51 (951 s), the YouTube video 977 s. All caption times and the site audio refer to the 977 s video, so do not reuse streaming-service timings.

The en-GB caption track was not retrieved; the Invidious mirror is flaky. The English translation mirrored on nasheedlyrics.com matches the official short word for word. Archive all three tracks in the repo (for example under work/karitas/), since YouTube blocks direct access.

Caption orthography kept verbatim, but the project may want to normalise it: «mâfiha» (critical editions: «mâfîhâ»), «arif» without â, a closing period in «kavga nedir.», the space in «و سِواكُم», «ياهو» written as one word. Decide whether the site keeps the artist's spelling or a scholarly one, and say which in sources.md.
Section times and texts in content/songs/karitas/lyrics.json (built for a 490 s recording) are obsolete. Replace them with the caption-based sequence above, then align at word level.
